requirement:
Outlining reads one file snapshot and parses its supplied bytes. Text search
lists files in scope and searches their bytes. Structural search lists files
in scope and parses their supplied snapshots. These operations share the
filesystem scope under {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`.
rationale:
The tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.provider_defaults.composition`.

**Outlining reads one snapshot and parses its bytes.**
- `sources/tests.rs#fn[defaults_use_provider_primitives_and_keep_one_parse_snapshot]` calls the default `parse` on a `Memory` provider.
- It asserts exactly one read (`reads == 1`).
- It then reads again and gets "version 1", while the parsed source and its outline still show "version 0". This shows the outline is built from the same supplied bytes as the source.
- `fn[list_read_only_provider_supports_selected_language_parse_and_structural_search]` shows the default parse over a provider that only supplies `list` and `read`. The outline resolves `fn[provided]` and the source text matches the supplied bytes.

**Text search lists files in scope and searches their bytes.**
- In the same `Memory` test, `search_text` with scope `src` records the event `list:src`, then a read of `src/one.txt`.
- The match excerpt is "version 2\nhit one\nhit two". That is the bytes of the third read, so the search ran on bytes supplied by `read`.
- The event sequence `["src/one.txt","src/one.txt","list:src","src/one.txt"]` is asserted exactly.

**Structural search lists files in scope and parses their supplied snapshots.**
- `fn[structural_search_uses_overridden_parses_their_snapshot_and_requested_scope]` uses `CachedParse`. Its `read` returns an error, so any refetch would fail.
- The test asserts the requested scope `src` is passed to `list` on every call.
- It asserts that the match path, selector and excerpt come from the parse, and that there are three parses across three calls.
- It covers `limit` values of none, 1 and 0.
- `fn[list_read_only_provider_supports_selected_language_parse_and_structural_search]` covers the default parse path with a list+read provider. It also covers a mismatched parsed resource producing an error, and language filtering.

**Shared filesystem scope under `local_provider`.**
- `tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository]` runs with and without a Git repository.
- It checks `list`, `read`, `parse` (outline) and `search_text`. That includes direct requests naming a file or subdirectory, nested ignore exceptions, `.git` exclusion and `..` rejection.
- `fn[built_in_languages_and_structural_search_use_the_project_scope]` covers structural search with the same scope. It checks an ignored file, an ignored directory, `.git`, a direct file scope and `..`.

I found no input class or failure case in the text that lacks a test with an assertion, and the acknowledgments list is empty.
